rules.indicatorName: Falling eGFR trend
rules.notes: Clinical-review trend monitor, not a QOF claim indicator. Observation history is required: where only the latest eGFR is available the chip shows no_data until multi-point history exists. NICE NG203 defines accelerated CKD progression as a sustained decrease in eGFR of >=15 mL/min/1.73m2 within 12 months (or >=25% with a change in GFR category). Window is 24 months to capture enough GP data points (annual bloods mean 12 months yields only 1-2 readings). Confirm a sustained fall on repeat testing and exclude AKI before acting.

rules.indicatorName: Raised potassium (hyperkalaemia)
rules.source: NICE CKS Hyperkalaemia / UK Kidney Association (2020)
rules.notes: Hyperkalaemia clinical-safety alert. AMBER 5.5-5.9 mmol/L (mild): first exclude pseudohyperkalaemia (haemolysed or delayed sample) and recheck; review contributing drugs (ACEi/ARB, MRA/spironolactone, potassium-sparing diuretics, NSAIDs, trimethoprim, potassium supplements) and dietary potassium. RED >=6.0 mmol/L (moderate to severe): arrange urgent same-day clinical assessment and a 12-lead ECG. K+ >=6.5 mmol/L, or any ECG changes (peaked T waves, broadened QRS), is a medical emergency - give IV calcium gluconate for cardioprotection, insulin-glucose +/- salbutamol, continuous ECG monitoring and urgent senior/renal input. Always identify and treat the underlying cause.

rules.indicatorName: Rising HbA1c trend (diabetes)
rules.source: NICE NG28 (type 2 diabetes in adults) / NICE NG17 (type 1 diabetes)
rules.notes: Clinical-review trend monitor for worsening glycaemic control in people on the diabetes register (fires only when the patient is on the DM register). Not a QOF claim indicator. Values are in mmol/mol (IFCC units). Multi-point HbA1c history is required: where only the latest result is available the chip shows no_data until history exists. Window is 24 months to capture enough readings (HbA1c is typically checked 3-6 monthly in diabetes). The >=10 mmol/mol rise is a pragmatic review threshold, not a fixed guideline cut-off - adjust to local policy. A sustained rise suggests deteriorating control: review adherence, diet/lifestyle, intercurrent illness or steroids, and consider treatment intensification per NICE NG28/NG17. Confirm on repeat testing and interpret alongside the individualised HbA1c target (commonly 48 mmol/mol, or 53 mmol/mol where treatment carries hypoglycaemia risk).

rules.indicatorName: Offer of referral to a weight-management programme in obesity

Numerator cluster confirmed 2026-08-28 against the official QOF v51 business rules (Obesity_v51.3, https://digital.nhs.uk/data-and-information/data-collections-and-data-sets/data-collections/quality-and-outcomes-framework-qof/business-rules/quality-and-outcomes-framework-qof-business-rules-v51-2026): cluster WTMGREF_COD "Weight management programme referral codes" (SNOMED refset 999037041000230107) — a single general referral cluster, not split by tier, so the existing tier-2/tier-3-worded match terms are a reasonable free-text approximation of it, not an under-match.
rules.notes: ENABLED 2026-08-28 (The Keeper) — was shipped disabled pending CSO confirmation of points/thresholds; that confirmation is now done (see source) so the stated blocker is resolved. rules.source: QOF 26/27 SMOK002 (NICE IND97); confirmed vs primary source PRN02356 2026-06-21
rules.notes: SMOK002 is a SINGLE QOF indicator (25 pts, 50-90%) covering smoking-status recording across CHD, PAD, stroke/TIA, hypertension, diabetes, COPD, CKD, asthma and SMI. Modelled as one per-register check so it surfaces for a patient on any qualifying register (the schema gates by a single register). QOF year floor (1 Apr - 31 Mar) applies. Replaces the pre-26/27 SMOK001 x8 model (The Keeper, 2026-06-21). 2026-09-28: achievement is the NHSD SMOK_COD refset (OpenCodelists nhsd-primary-care-domain-refsets/smok_cod/20260630, 71 concept ids). LSMOK_COD, EXSMOK_COD and NSMOK_COD are subsets of it. Cigarette consumption (230056004), tobacco smoking consumption (266918002), cigar consumption (230057008), pipe tobacco consumption (230058003), waterpipe tobacco consumption (836001000000109), stopped smoking (160617001), date ceased smoking (160625004), smoking reduced (134406006), smokes tobacco daily (449868002), cigarette pack-years (401201003), smoker (77176002), ex-smoker (8517006), never smoked tobacco (266919005) and cigarette smoker (65568007) are in that refset. Text look-fors cover the preferred terms that do not already contain a shorter status phrase, so a text-only row still counts. The substring smoking status is not a look-for: it matches 1098881000000103 Declined to give smoking status. tobacco use matches 11351000175103 Tobacco use screening declined. smoking cessation matches advice, referral and pharmacotherapy (SMOKADV_COD, REFERSSSA_COD, PHARM_COD). nicotine dependence (56294008) is not in SMOK_COD. Those concept ids are in snomedExclude, and the phrases are text excludes, with the existing passive exclude kept. A dashboard row named exactly Smoking status is read from its value (Ex-smoker), not from the wrapper words. PCA codes 716391000000109 (patient unsuitable) and 717771000000108 (informed dissent) suppress the chip when the numerator is not already met; they do not count as achieved. Not in this build: a never-smoker code recorded after the 25th birthday carries forward, and an ex-smoker code carries forward for three years. The journal feed is about 400 days, so a three-year-old ex-smoker code is not visible here. Both stay follow-ups. The newest matching date wins.
